moduleTitle: Module 3. Sensory, Motor, Autonomic and Endocrine Physiology

competencies.name: Sensory transduction
competencies.can: Explain how a stimulus is converted into a receptor potential and how that graded potential becomes a train of action potentials in the sensory neuron.

competencies.name: Receptor classification
competencies.can: Classify a receptor by stimulus type as a mechanoreceptor, chemoreceptor, thermoreceptor, photoreceptor, or nociceptor and give a body location for each.

competencies.name: Stimulus coding
competencies.can: Explain how the nervous system encodes modality, location, intensity, and duration and identify the labeled line principle.

competencies.name: Receptive fields and acuity
competencies.can: Relate receptive field size and lateral inhibition to two point discrimination and predict which body regions have the finest acuity.

competencies.name: Receptor adaptation
competencies.can: Distinguish tonic from phasic receptors by their adaptation rate and match each to a stimulus the body needs to monitor continuously or only at onset.

competencies.name: Somatosensory pathways
competencies.can: Trace touch and pain information from receptor to cortex and explain why the somatosensory homunculus is disproportionate.

competencies.name: Pain and its modulation
competencies.can: Distinguish fast and slow pain by fiber type, explain referred pain by convergence, and describe how gate control and endogenous opioids reduce pain transmission.

competencies.name: Tactile mapping and adaptation testing
competencies.can: Measure two point discrimination at several body sites and show receptor adaptation and referred sensation experimentally.
